channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD declines to near $58.40 as US Dollar regains ground
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is down almost 1% to near $58.40 during the Asian trading session on Friday. The white metal faces selling pressure as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds slightly, attempting to snap a three-day losing streak.

item.title: Bank of Japan holds interest rate steady at 1.00% as expected
item.description: The Bank of Japan (BoJ) board members decided to leave the short-term interest rate unadjusted at 1.00%, following the conclusion of its two-day monetary policy review meeting on Friday.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens as Bank of Japan holds rates at 1%
item.description: USD/JPY rises after two days of losses, trading around 160.80 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair continues to appreciate as the Japanese Yen (JPY) weakens following the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) decision to keep its short-term interest rate unchanged at 1.00%.

item.title: EUR/JPY rallies further above 185.00 against Japanese Yen after BoJ’s policy decision
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends the intraday rally to near 185.20 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) after the Bank of Japan’ (BoJ) monetary policy decision during the Asian trading session on Friday. The BoJ has kept interest rates steady at 1%, as expected, with an 8-1 majority.

item.title: British Pound falls as US Dollar receives from internal FOMC policy split
item.description: GBP/USD loses ground after three days of gains, trading around 1.3450 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair depreciates as the US Dollar (USD) gains support from a hawkish pause by the Federal Reserve (Fed) and an internal FOMC policy split.

item.title: Australian Dollar inches lower as China’s NBS Manufacturing PMI falls in July
item.description: AUD/USD inches lower after registering over 1% gains in the previous day, trading around 0.7020 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair remains subdued following the release of disappointing Chinese Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Climbs back above mid-160.00s as BoJ rate decision looms
item.description: The USD/JPY pair is seen building on the previous day's late recovery from sub-158.00 levels, or the lowest since May 14, and gaining positive traction during the Asian session on Friday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds losses following China PMI data
item.description: NZD/USD loses ground after three days of gains, trading around 0.5870 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair remains subdued following the release of China's Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) data.

item.title: United States Dollar Index bounces off its lowest level since June 17, back above 100.00
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, gains some positive traction and climbs back above the 100.00 psychological mark during the Asian session on Friday.

item.title: China's NBS Manufacturing PMI falls to 49.2 in July, Non-Manufacturing PMI eases to 49.0
item.description: China’s Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 49.2 in July, compared to 50.3 in the previous reading, China’s National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) reported on Friday. The reading came in below the market consensus of 50.0 in the reported month.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7894 vs. 6.7892 previous
item.description: On Friday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7894 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7892.

item.title: Euro softens to near 1.1500 as US-Iran war widens
item.description: The EUR/ USD pair loses ground to near 1.1515 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. The Euro (EUR) softens against the US Dollar (USD) amid risk-off sentiment and fears of wider war in the Middle East.

item.title: WTI holds losses around $82.50 on renewed US-Iran diplomatic hopes
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price remains in the negative territory for the second successive day, trading around $82.60 per barrel during the Asian hours on Friday. Crude oil prices have lost ground following renewed hopes for a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran conflict.

item.title: Japan’s Mimura: Always prepared to take suitable measures
item.description: Atsushi Mimura, Japan’s Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs and top foreign exchange official, said on Friday that he is in close contact with relevant authorities on foreign exchange, adding that the officials are always prepared to take suitable measures.

item.title: US President Donald Trump says Board of Peace has reached agreement for disarmament of Hamas
item.description: US President Donald Trump claimed his Board of Peace has reached an “historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza,”the Guardian reported on Friday.

item.title: Iran says US to ‘pay the price’ for Qeshm civilians killed
item.description: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said that the United States (US) will pay the price for killing Iranian civilians, Aljazeera reported on Thursday.

item.title: Saudi Arabia announces maritime defence alliance to protect Red Sea
item.description: Saudi Arabia and 13 other countries announced the creation of an international coalition to safeguard freedom of navigation through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, Reuters reported on Thursday.

item.title: The Japanese Yen gets its ambush, and the Bank of Japan gets overnight to justify it
item.description: USD/JPY trades just above 159.50, down 2.31% and more than five Yen below a high set just short of 164.00.

item.title: Japan’s Tokyo CPI inflation rises to 2.0% YoY in July
item.description: The headline Tokyo Consumer Price Index (CPI) for July rose 2.0% YoY as compared to 1.7% in the previous month, the Statistics Bureau of Japan showed on Friday.

item.title: Gold edges higher above $4,100 as traders trim Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) gains momentum to around $4,110 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal edges higher as traders reduce their bets on interest rate hikes a day after Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh offered little clarity on policy.

item.title: The Australian Dollar clears a big figure on an intervention it will come to regret
item.description: AUD/USD trades above 0.7000, up 1.06% and roughly 85 pips clear of a session low set just below 0.6950 in the early European hours. The advance cut through the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) sitting at 0.7000, a level the pair has been rejected at repeatedly since June.

item.title: British Pound Sterling rallies on a hawkish vote the Bank of England immediately talked down
item.description: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% for a fifth straight meeting on Thursday, and the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) got there on a 6-3 vote, with three members backing an immediate quarter-point increase against a consensus that had looked for 7-2.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: 50-day SMA guards bullish structure
item.description: The USD/CHF retreats for the second straight day, down more than 1% amid growing speculation of an intervention in the FX markets, which boosted the Japanese Yen. The pair fell to a 10-day low of 0.8039, slightly above the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at 0.8027.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar extends sell-off after weak US growth, Yen surges on suspected intervention
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) falls sharply during the American session on Thursday after United States economic growth missed expectations and underlying inflation moderated.

item.title: China: Incremental support and trade risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Senior Asia Economist Alex Loo assesses the July Politburo meeting, noting no major new stimulus despite acknowledged growth challenges. The focus is on fiscal execution, accelerating spending and bond use to support the Six Networks infrastructure program.

item.title: Oil: Key driver of UK inflation scenarios – Rabobank
item.description: RaboResearch highlights Oil as the dominant input for UK monetary policy. The Bank of England’s central forecast assumes Oil prices fall from $76 to around $71, with inflation peaking near 3.2%, but Brent already trades above $90.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Gradual gains versus US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank FX & Commodity Analyst Volkmar Baur argues that China’s large trade surplus, driven increasingly by green technology exports, is supporting a stronger Chinese Yuan.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG eyes $60.00 as rebound builds
item.description: Silver price advances for the second straight day and hits a three-day high above $59.00mid growing speculation of intervention in the foreign exchange markets, to boost the Yen, and weaken the Greenback.

item.title: Gold jumps as suspected Yen intervention crushes US Dollar as Fed bets ease
item.description: Gold price advances some 0.92% on Thursday after the US Dollar drops following a suspected intervention in the foreign exchange markets, with the Japanese Yen hitting a near two-month high versus the Greenback. The XAU/USD trades at $4,100 after bouncing off the low of the day (LOD) at $4,028.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Political risks rise as fundamentals hold firm – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan highlights that Malaysia’s solid growth, low inflation and prudent policy are supporting the Ringgit, but rising domestic political risks could drive USD/MYR in coming months.
